summary: Frontend-only retest of the GlicoTrack repeated-edit regression after switching the edit-intent mechanism from URL params (expo-router) to an external module store built on useSyncExternalStore (/app/frontend/src/editStore.ts). THE REGRESSION IS STILL PRESENT. Only the FIRST edit of any session succeeds; the 2nd and all subsequent edits silently fail: tapping edit-button navigates back to Inserisci but edit-banner never appears, the glucose field stays empty, the header stays 'Nuova Misurazione' and the save button stays 'Salva Misurazione'. Reproduced across multiple sub-cases: (A) 1st edit of any row from a fresh session -> PASS; (B) 2nd edit (another row) after cancel-edit-button on the 1st -> FAIL; (C) 2nd edit of the same row after cancel -> FAIL; (D) 2nd edit after a real update save -> FAIL. All other flows PASS: add 2 measurements via default web-date-input/web-time-input works; update does NOT duplicate rows (count stays 2); past-date add via GG/MM/AAAA + HH:MM works; delete-button -> delete-confirm-modal -> confirm-delete-button removes while cancel-delete-button keeps; export-pdf-button calls window.print without crash; empty-data export shows the 'Nessun dato da esportare' info toast; glucose dynamic color (green/orange/red based on value) and the form-error validation on empty glucose work. No red-screen; only cosmetic 'shadow*' and 'props.pointerEvents' deprecation warnings from react-native-web.

ui_bugs.component: Inserisci screen edit-intent consumer (useEffect in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:87-100 that reads useEditRequest() and calls clearEditRequest())
ui_bugs.issue: REGRESSION NOT FIXED. The external-store approach still fails for every edit after the first. Reproducible RCA: the useEffect synchronously calls clearEditRequest() AFTER it prefills the form. clearEditRequest() mutates editingRequestId -> null and emit()s. Because Inserimento subscribes to that same store via useSyncExternalStore, this emit happens WHILE the component is still committing the first edit; React re-runs the effect with editRequestId=null (early-return). After that first edit, the subscriber appears to get into a state where subsequent store transitions (null -> newId caused by Storico's requestEdit) do NOT re-trigger the prefill effect: in TEST B (edit row1 after cancel), TEST C (edit row2 again after cancel) and TEST D (edit row1 after a successful update save) the banner stays hidden and the form stays empty. Only the first edit of a page-load works, matching the exact scenario we were asked to retest. Evidence: TEST A banner=True glucose=120; TEST B banner=False glucose=''; TEST C banner=False glucose=''; TEST D banner=False glucose=''.

integration_issues.flow: Repeated edit from Storico -> Inserisci (2nd and later edits, incl. edit-after-cancel and edit-after-update)
integration_issues.issue: Mutating the external store from inside the subscribing component's useEffect (clearEditRequest()) is unreliable with useSyncExternalStore. Recommended fix: make the store value a monotonically-changing token so that even the same id re-fires AND stop calling clearEditRequest inside the effect. Concrete design that will work: in /app/frontend/src/editStore.ts expose `{ id: string | null, token: number }` (increment token in every requestEdit, including when id is the same). In Inserisci use `const req = useEditRequest();` and a `const lastTokenRef = useRef(0)`; the useEffect depends on `[req.token, data]`; when `req.token !== lastTokenRef.current && req.id && (m = data.find(x=>x.id===req.id))` -> prefill AND set `lastTokenRef.current = req.token` WITHOUT mutating the store. On save/cancel do NOT clear the store; just reset the ref/local state. Because the ref gate prevents reapplying, there's no need to clear. This removes the mid-effect store mutation that is tripping up the current implementation.

action_items: FIX HIGH regression (repeated edits): refactor /app/frontend/src/editStore.ts to emit a {id, token} snapshot with an always-incrementing token, and in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx drive the prefill off a `lastTokenRef` gate instead of calling clearEditRequest() inside the useEffect. Also stop calling clearEditRequest() from onSave/cancelEdit for the same reason. (See 'integration_issues' above for a concrete code sketch.)

After fix, retest the EXACT scenario from the request: add glucose 120 Prima Pranzo and glucose 90 Notte -> edit row 1 (banner, header 'Modifica Misurazione', save 'Aggiorna Misurazione', change 120 -> 200, save) -> edit row 2 (MUST enter edit mode with row 2 values) -> cancel -> edit row 1 (MUST enter edit mode again, glucose = 200). All three edits must succeed.

Keep testIDs stable: edit-button-<id>, edit-banner, cancel-edit-button, save-measurement-button, glucose-input, delete-button-<id>, delete-confirm-modal, confirm-delete-button, cancel-delete-button, export-pdf-button.
(Optional, non-blocking) web-date-input currently allows future dates; iOS/Android use maximumDate=new Date(). Consider matching on web.
critical_code_review_comments: src/editStore.ts: calling emit() for the same id is correct, but useSyncExternalStore relies on Object.is(getSnapshot()) to decide if it must schedule an update; a bare string snapshot CAN still trigger when id differs, but is fragile. A token-based snapshot removes that fragility.

app/(tabs)/index.tsx:87-100: mutating the external store (clearEditRequest) INSIDE a useEffect that subscribes to that same store is the proximate cause. The emit fires synchronously, React re-reads the snapshot during commit, and subsequent transitions from the store appear to be dropped by the subscriber in web react-native. Avoid mid-effect store mutation entirely.
app/(tabs)/storico.tsx:126-131 edit onPress (requestEdit + router.navigate('/')) is fine and does not need to change.
useUpdateMeasurement path is correct: updating an existing id does NOT duplicate rows (verified: count stayed at 2 after a save).

success_rate.frontend: ~83% (5/6 required flows pass; the HIGH repeated-edit regression is still blocking)

seed_data_creation: Ephemeral AsyncStorage/localStorage measurements created during each run and cleared via window.localStorage.clear() at the start of each test cycle.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Minimal repro (confirmed on preview https://insulin-daily.preview.emergentagent.com, viewport 390x844): (1) clear localStorage, reload. (2) In Inserisci add two measurements (any two; e.g. 120 Prima Pranzo, 90 Notte). (3) Open Storico (tap bottom 'Storico' tab). (4) Tap pencil (edit-button-<id>) on the FIRST row -> edit-banner shows, form is prefilled, header is 'Modifica Misurazione', save label 'Aggiorna Misurazione'. This PASSES. (5) Tap cancel-edit-button (or save after a change). (6) Open Storico again. (7) Tap pencil on ANY row (same or different) -> edit-banner is NOT shown, form is empty, header is 'Nuova Misurazione'. This FAILS. Also failing: (A) edit row2 first (works), cancel, edit row1 -> fails. (B) edit row1, save update, edit row1 again -> fails. Only ever the first edit succeeds. The fix must change editStore.ts to emit a monotonically-increasing token, and index.tsx to gate the prefill on a lastTokenRef instead of mutating the store from inside its own useEffect.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: useSyncExternalStore subscriber in Inserimento mutates the same store (clearEditRequest -> null + emit) synchronously inside the useEffect that reacts to the subscription. React's commit-phase re-reads getSnapshot during that emit and, in react-native-web, subsequent emit()s from the store (null -> newId when Storico calls requestEdit) are not reliably delivered to the subscriber - the prefill useEffect never re-fires for the 2nd and later edits. Reproduces 100% across edit-after-cancel and edit-after-update. The fix is to (a) make requestEdit emit a {id, token} where token always increases (so even identical ids are observable transitions) and (b) stop calling clearEditRequest() from inside the subscriber's useEffect / from onSave/cancelEdit; instead gate the one-shot consumption with a useRef(lastToken).
